answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence costly: require every account to lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit bids or vote, then slash that deposit when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. A Sybil attacker may mint a thousand names, but each must tie up capital, and detected accounts lose it; splitting one identity into many no longer multiplies influence for free. The zenith of protection comes from fair, auditable challenges, while a raven watcher can trace a thread of linked payouts and trigger review without treating shared ownership alone as proof.
